note: Authoritative local data from L1 chains.db (DeFiLlama + CoinGecko + growthepie/Dune). Raw signals, no scores. null = NO DATA (do not guess). FRESHNESS: price & market caps are live (today); TVL/stablecoin LEVELS are the latest available (carried forward if a chain's today-point isn't in yet); daily-FLOW metrics (DEX volume, fees, active_addresses, tx_count) are the LAST COMPLETE UTC DAY (today is partial and excluded) — full-day figures, use them as-is. SHARES are each chain's % of the WHOLE DeFi market (all ~500 chains; denominators in market.total_*), so tracked chains sum to <100% and deltas are immune to which chains we track. TVL/volume are USD-denominated, so share moves in a big market swing partly reflect token price, not pure flows. Each chain ALSO carries its OWN raw TVL growth — tvl_change_1d/7d/30d_pct (chain's level vs itself N days ago); use THESE for 'is this chain's TVL growing', NOT the share deltas (share = slice of market, a different question). If tvl_suspect_1d is true the 1d move is a likely upstream data glitch (a >25% one-day swing) — discount the 1d figure and lean on the 7d/30d trend instead. Stablecoins mirror this: stable_change_1d/7d/30d_pct are the chain's OWN stablecoin-supply trend (use for 'is stablecoin capital arriving/leaving', and to confirm or debunk 'stables doubled/halved' claims); stable_suspect_1d flags a >30% one-day swing as a likely DeFiLlama adapter flap (a bridged asset dropping in/out of the index) — call it out as a data-quality event, not a capital flow, and lean on 7d/30d. N-days-ago baselines are median-smoothed, so a one-day glitch can't fake a 7d/30d trend.

## Sui v1.84.2: mainnet hotfix

#### Sui Protocol Version in this release: `142`

**Validators**
- Fixes a fork in the address-balance funds withdraw scheduler. **This only affects validators, and only those whose checkpoint execution runs ahead of their consensus path (lagging validators); validators that are keeping up are not affected. Full nodes are not affected.** On a lagging validator, the scheduler could drop reservations for accounts it was already tracking. A later withdraw could then be approved locally but rejected by the committee, forking that validator. Skipped batches now keep their reservations until settlement. ([#28693](https://github.com/MystenLabs/sui/pull/28693), from [#28679](https://github.com/MystenLabs/sui/pull/28679))
  - **Validators should upgrade to v1.84.2 promptly.** No protocol change: the protocol version stays **142**, with no config changes.

#### Full Log: https://github.com/MystenLabs/sui/commits/mainnet-v1.84.2

`v2.11.2` improves peer connection management and peer activity visibility. It also includes a sequence-store block production fix and dependency updates. This promotes the code tested in `v2.11.2-beta3` to stable. 

## Highlights

- **Silent peer cleanup:** removes peers that remain silent when connection capacity is under pressure. Defaults are 75% occupancy, a 10-minute grace period, at most one removal per minute and a 5-minute reconnect cooldown. Static and trusted peers are protected. These settings are configurable under `[p2p]`.
- **Request-only peer cleanup:** extends rotation to eligible inbound peers that only request data when inbound connections have been refused for lack of capacity. Recent useful contributions protect a peer for 30 minutes. This shares the silent-peer removal budget and cooldown.
- **Peer reputation visibility:** exposes activity and scores through `admin_peers`, aggregate metrics and score-transition logs. Per-peer metrics are disabled by default. Abuse scores remain observational; connection cleanup uses the separate activity policy.
- **Fork compatibility:** future Bor hardforks participate in the ETH fork ID while preserving compatibility for forks already known to released binaries.
- **Sequence-store producers:** avoids rebuilding a producer's own block when the store has acknowledged an entry but its read path has not yet applied it.
- **Dependencies:** Go 1.26.11 and `klauspost/compress` v1.20.2.

## Overview

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This is a recommended release for all operators, and a strongly recommended one for operators whose virtual nodes peer through `--p2p.static` with `--p2p.no-discovery`. It contains a fix for static peers that change IP address, and embedded configs for three new devnets.

## Chain Configuration

- **sepolia-devnet-4, -5 and -6 added** (#24054). These are OP Labs devnets on Sepolia used to rehearse upcoming network upgrades, listed in the [superchain registry](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/blob/main/CHAINS.md). Virtual nodes can now start `sepolia-devnet-4` (`420130019`), `sepolia-devnet-5` (`420130020`) and `sepolia-devnet-6` (`420130021`) by name, with `--vn.<chainID>.network`, instead of an explicit rollup config and genesis. A node on an earlier release still needs the explicit config for these chains. No other chain's config changes in this release.

## Other changes

### Bug fixes

- A virtual node can now reconnect to a `p2p.static` peer that returns on a new IP after the node has been up for more than 7 days. Before, the configured static-peer addresses expired after 7 days, and the node dialed only the peer's old address. With discovery disabled, the node then stopped receiving unsafe payloads until it was restarted, and followed L1 derivation only. A `/dns4` static-peer address is now resolved again on every reconnect. Nodes using discovery were not affected (#23946)

**Full Changelog**: …[truncated]

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Base Mainnet:** Required upgrade and migration by mid August.
> **Base Sepolia:** Highly recommended upgrade and migration.
> **Migration time:** Migrations may take a while, we strongly suggest you start mainnet as soon as possible.
> **V1 Snapshots:** Will be decommissioned over the next few weeks.

### base-reth-node
- **Reth V2 Snapshots** To benefit from V2, you must both update to 1.2.0 and update your database to use v2 storage. You can do this via:
  * **Recommended:** Download a new snapshot `base-reth-node download`. See the [docs](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/node-operators/snapshots) for more information.
  * Migrate your existing V1 data `base-reth-node db migrate-v2`. Note: `migrate-v2` is expected to take **much** longer than `download`. Non-archival nodes are not supported for this command.
- **Upgrades Reth to v2.3.0**
- Bug fixes and stability improvements

### base-consensus
- **Fixed prune node sync**: Nodes can reliably do a pruned node sync from genesis
- Bug fixes and stability improvements

_This proposal is part of the protocol fee rollout, following proposals #93, #94, #95, #96, #99, #100, and #102. It uses the expedited governance process approved in UNIfication, where fee parameter update proposals can bypass the RFC stage and go directly to a five-day Snapshot followed by an onchain vote._

v4 protocol fees went live in July and are now active on eight chains: Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base, OP Mainnet, BNB Chain, Polygon, Robinhood Chain, and Arc. With the upgraded v4 fee adapter proposed in [this Snapshot,](https://snapshot.org/#/s:uniswapgovernance.eth/proposal/0x65503933c85b5c813a350603a6f4be143e911f073ae17ff109aa978f494ae4bc) this proposal extends v4 protocol fees to the five remaining chains where v2 and v3 fees are already live, so all fee-active chains run the same v4 fee system.

This proposal:

-   Enables v4 protocol fees on Celo, Soneium, X Layer, World Chain, and Zora
    
-   Uses the same upgraded `V4FeeAdapter` and initial configuration as proposed in [INSERT: 104 snapshot]
    
-   Lowers the target LP fee on the two USDC/USDG StablePair pools on Arbitrum

governance.title: Upgrade the v4 Protocol Fee Adapter
governance.body:
_This proposal is part of the protocol fee rollout, following proposals #93, #94, #95, #96, #99, #100, and #102. It uses the expedited governance process approved in UNIfication, where fee parameter update proposals can bypass the RFC stage and go directly to a five-day Snapshot followed by an onchain vote._

v4 protocol fees went live in July, and v4 now accounts for roughly half of Uniswap volume. Much of that growth comes from hooks, which let builders launch new pools with custom behavior. Hooks are very diverse: some use static LP fees, some use dynamic fees, and some use custom accounting to govern swap behavior.

The initial protocol fee controller for V4 doesn't have the expressivity required to deal with all the different types of hooks popping up in the ecosystem. This proposal upgrades the v4 fee logic so governance can set fees for any hook through flexible and reusable rules. The upgraded logic also gives hooks a direct way to opt into the protocol fee themselves and set appropriate fees for their pools.

governance.title: [7.5] [Social] IPS Amendment No. 2: IPS Amendment Authority
governance.body:
## Summary

[Next Era of ENS DAO: Empowering the ENS Foundation](https://discuss.ens.domains/t/next-era-of-ens-dao-empowering-the-ens-foundation/22329) put the Endowment and the Endowment Manager relationship with the ENS Foundation. The current [Investment Policy Statement (IPS v2.0, EP 6.46)](https://tomato-careful-otter-747.mypinata.cloud/ipfs/bafybeigwpq44fxgxjgst7yskemkawcb7v4leh3pez5e23gsoox55b6mpa4) states only a DAO vote can change the policy and names MetaGov as the oversight body.

This proposal amends the IPS to reflect the roles already ratified in Next Era. The Foundation Board can amend the IPS by resolution after a 7-day forum discussion, and the Foundation replaces the Meta-Governance Working Group as oversight body and counterparty to the Endowment Manager.

Importantly, the DAO retains the Minimum Runway and the authority to make changes to Section 3, so the Foundation cannot alter the amendment process or its own role. The DAO can also reverse any Board amendment by Social Proposal.

governance.title: [7.4] [Social] IPS Amendment No. 1: Endowment Options Overlay
governance.body:
About this Proposal
This proposal amends the ENS Endowment Investment Policy Statement (IPS v2.0, EP 6.46) to permit covered options writing as part of the Endowment's scheduled rebalancing, within limits written into the policy.

It relaxes one existing constraint: options written in the direction of a required rebalance are treated as ETH/stablecoin rebalancing under Section 5, not as speculative trading. No other constraint is relaxed, and the Minimum Runway and its priority are unchanged.

This vote is a policy change only. It grants no onchain permissions. The Endowment Manager's permissions on any options venue are granted separately through a Permissions Update Request, reviewed by Blockful and moved to execution at the discretion of the ENS Foundation Board.
For Delegates:
The discussion, including the 10 November update, is on the forum thread.
The methodology, backtest and rationale for each limit are in Expanding the Endowment Mandate: Onchain Options. That thread and the amendment thread together form KPK's written rationale under IPS Section 3.
On passing, the consolidated text will be published as IPS v2.1, pinned to IPFS and shared on the governance forum for record …[truncated]

Expand the CSMC Mandate to Cover Additional Penalty Cases
governance.body:
### Summary

This proposal seeks approval to adopt an updated mandate for [the Community Staking Module Committee (CSMC)](https://docs.lido.fi/multisigs/committees#29-community-staking-module-committee), which oversees [operational responsibilities](https://research.lido.fi/t/community-staking-module-committee/8333) for both 0x01 and 0x02 [Community Staking Modules (CSM).](https://docs.lido.fi/staking-modules/contracts/CSModule) 

The principal change is to extend the circumstances in which the CSMC may apply the existing General Delayed Penalty mechanism beyond MEV stealing, to include additional penalties associated with validator slashing and other incidents that may adversely affect the protocol. By doing so, the proposal does not introduce a new penalty mechanism, but rather expands the authorized uses of the existing mechanism.

### Background

The CSMC was established to handle operational actions that may require frequent execution or rapid response, including MEV stealing penalty management, Node Operator bond curve adjustments, module parameter changes, and emergency interventions.
